History:
• Chief complaint: Painful urination (dysuria) × 6 days.  
• Course: Gradual onset; persists every void.  
• Associated symptoms:  
  – Foul-smelling urine.  
  – Intermittent mid-line lower abdominal pain, 7/10 intensity, comes and goes.  
  – Small spots of blood in urine during same 6-day period.  
• Negatives: No fever (subjective, no thermometer available), no flank/loin or lower back pain, no change in bowel habit, no vaginal discharge, eating and drinking normally.  
• First episode; no recent dehydration, excessive exercise, or increased sexual activity reported.

Past Medical History:
• Irritable bowel syndrome (IBS).  
• Medications: Mebeverine 200 mg orally three times daily.  
• Drug allergies: Clindamycin (reaction not detailed).  
• No past kidney/urinary infections, surgeries, or other chronic illnesses reported.  
• Family history: Non-contributory per patient.  
• Social: Lives with friends; support worker. Alcohol ≈1 glass wine/week; non-smoker.

Physical Examination:
• Telehealth encounter; no direct examination performed.  
• Patient alert, oriented, conversational.  
• Reports no fever; vitals not measured.  
• No reported flank tenderness or costovertebral angle pain.  
• Abdominal pain present but localized to mid-lower abdomen; not assessed physically.

Impression:
• Likely acute uncomplicated lower urinary tract infection (cystitis).

Management Plan:
• Prescribed 3-day course of oral antibiotic (name/dose/route/frequency not documented) sent electronically to Knightsbridge Pharmacy.  
• Hydration: Encourage 2.5–3 L water daily.  
• Adjuncts: Consider cranberry juice and over-the-counter urinary alkalinizing sachets (details to be provided in notes).  
• Monitoring: Purchase thermometer and check temperature periodically.  
• Safety-netting: Seek medical review if pain worsens, flank/back pain develops, fever occurs, difficulty passing urine, or symptoms persist/recur after antibiotics.  
• Routine follow-up not required if symptoms resolve.

Patient Summary:
Susan (DOB ‎04/02/1974) presents with 6-day history of dysuria, malodorous urine, minor hematuria, and intermittent suprapubic pain. Findings are consistent with an uncomplicated cystitis; 3-day oral antibiotic prescribed with hydration and safety advice.

Key Takeaways:
• Start antibiotic course today and complete full 3 days.  
• Drink ≥2.5 L fluids daily; consider cranberry juice and alkalinizing sachets.  
• Buy a thermometer and monitor for fever; contact doctor if symptoms worsen or do not improve.

Next Steps:
• Collect prescription from Knightsbridge Pharmacy within the hour.  
• Monitor symptoms; if no improvement or any red-flag signs (fever, flank pain, urinary retention), arrange urgent reassessment.  
• If UTIs become recurrent, schedule further evaluation.

Quality checks:
• Missing expected elements: No recorded vitals (temp, HR, BP), no urinalysis, no antibiotic name/dose, no documented reaction type for clindamycin allergy.  
• Internal conflicts: None noted.  
• Transcript quality: Clear audio; minor repetition, no major inaudible sections.
